messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: advi - fullrank option broken?
parts: I was trying out advi on some dynamic modeling problems, but no matter the tolerance, step size, or samples used for computing the elbo, I end up with biased parameters. I wanted to try the fullrank option instead of meanfield, but this always generates crazy huge elbo's and doesn't seem to head towards convergence. Is this a known problem, or is it possible that fullrank ignores specified inits or something? I understand advi is still experimental...

messages.author: 453ddfeccaf29bbb
messages.subject: Re: advi - fullrank option broken?
parts:
hi charles,

thank you for your message.

would it be possible for you to share more details about your model? (if that's possible, of course.)

the fullrank version of advi is indeed experimental; we were able to successfully apply it to a small stochastic volatility model in our paper, but i'd love to learn more about how it's failing on your end. (http://www.proditus.com/papers/KucukelbirTran_2016.pdf)

regarding your concerns: i am not aware of any programming/implementation-level bug that specifically affects the fullrank version of advi. i reckon that the optimization for fullrank is more challenging than meanfield for your model and that the heuristic `eta` that we estimate is likely too large.

cheers,
alp

messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: Re: advi - fullrank option broken?
parts: I've been trying hierarchical multivariate auto / cross regressive time series, in both discrete and continuous time forms, using a Kalman filter to marginalise out latent states. Based on your comments I did a little more testing, and after further restricting the model / data I got fullrank to converge, though, in 15000 iterations rather than meanfield's 500. Regarding the eta estimation, it sometimes couldn't find an appropriate eta and sometimes suggested .1, so I just set it to that. I still seem to have some estimation inconsistency with full hmc for these models, probably the difficulties are related - it just seemed odd to me that meanfield would be so close to the final elbo straight away, and fullrank so far. If it still bugs me once I am more comfortable with the full model specification, I'll post again with the model / data. Just to know though, is it expected that fullrank would be orders of magnitude more difficult / slow? Based on current tentative results for these models I think NUTS is faster, though I'd also be interested in trying the stochastic sampling approach for large scale data at some point...

messages.author: 453ddfeccaf29bbb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: advi - fullrank option broken?
parts:
hi charles,

it's hard to tell when meanfield vs. fullrank gives an easier
optimization problem. this is an open research question.

it could be that the meanfield problem has a local optimum that is
close to the initialization; that would explain the fast
"convergence".

in terms of speed: p = # of parameters in your model. meanfield is
o(p), fullrank is o(p^2).

cheers,
alp
